channel.title: Aggregated External AI & Tech News
channel.description: Merged headlines from configured external sources

item.title: Users flock to open source Moltbot for always-on AI, despite major risks (Source: feeds.arstechnica.com)
item.description: The open source "Jarvis" chats via WhatsApp but requires access to your files and accounts.

item.title: Report: China approves import of high-end Nvidia AI chips after weeks of uncertainty (Source: feeds.arstechnica.com)
item.description: Over 400,000 H200 chips coming to tech giants as China tries to balance tech needs with self-reliance.

item.title: Site catering to online criminals has been seized by the FBI (Source: feeds.arstechnica.com)
item.description: One of the last holdouts for ransomware discussions, RAMP is taken down.

item.title: Does Anthropic believe its AI is conscious, or is that just what it wants Claude to think? (Source: feeds.arstechnica.com)
item.description: We have no proof that AI models suffer, but Anthropic acts like they might for training purposes.

item.title: County pays $600,000 to pentesters it arrested for assessing courthouse security (Source: feeds.arstechnica.com)
item.description: Settlement comes more than 6 years after Gary DeMercurio and Justin Wynn's ordeal began.

item.title: Developers say AI coding tools work-and that's precisely what worries them (Source: feeds.arstechnica.com)
item.description: Ars spoke to several software devs about AI and found enthusiasm tempered by unease.

item.title: AI agents now have their own Reddit-style social network, and it's getting weird fast (Source: feeds.arstechnica.com)
item.description: Moltbook lets 32,000 AI bots trade jokes, tips, and complaints about humans.

item.title: Notepad++ users take note: It's time to check if you're hacked (Source: feeds.arstechnica.com)
item.description: Suspected China-state hackers used update infrastructure to deliver backdoored version.

item.title: The rise of Moltbook suggests viral AI prompts may be the next big security threat (Source: feeds.arstechnica.com)
item.description: We don't need self-replicating AI models to have problems, just self-replicating prompts.

item.title: Nvidia's $100 billion OpenAI deal has seemingly vanished (Source: feeds.arstechnica.com)
item.description: Two AI giants shake market confidence after investment fails to materialize.

item.title: So yeah, I vibe-coded a log colorizer-and I feel good about it (Source: feeds.arstechnica.com)
item.description: Some semi-unhinged musings on where LLMs fit into my life-and how I'll keep using them.

item.title: Should AI chatbots have ads? Anthropic says no. (Source: feeds.arstechnica.com)
item.description: ChatGPT competitor comes out swinging with Super Bowl ad mocking AI product pitches.

item.title: Microsoft releases urgent Office patch. Russian-state hackers pounce. (Source: feeds.arstechnica.com)
item.description: The window to patch vulnerabilities is shrinking rapidly.

item.title: Increase of AI bots on the Internet sparks arms race (Source: feeds.arstechnica.com)
item.description: Publishers are rolling out more aggressive defenses.

item.title: OpenAI is hoppin' mad about Anthropic's new Super Bowl TV ads (Source: feeds.arstechnica.com)
item.description: Sam Altman calls AI competitor "dishonest" and "authoritarian" in lengthy post on X.

item.title: AI companies want you to stop chatting with bots and start managing them (Source: feeds.arstechnica.com)
item.description: Claude Opus 4.6 and OpenAI Frontier pitch a future of supervising AI agents.

item.title: Malicious packages for dYdX cryptocurrency exchange empties user wallets (Source: feeds.arstechnica.com)
item.description: Incident is at least the third time the exchange has been targeted by thieves.

item.title: Sixteen Claude AI agents working together created a new C compiler (Source: feeds.arstechnica.com)
item.description: The $20,000 experiment compiled a Linux kernel but needed deep human management.

item.title: OpenAI researcher quits over ChatGPT ads, warns of "Facebook" path (Source: feeds.arstechnica.com)
item.description: Zoë Hitzig resigned on the same day OpenAI began testing ads in its chatbot.

item.title: Once-hobbled Lumma Stealer is back with lures that are hard to resist (Source: feeds.arstechnica.com)
item.description: ClickFix bait, combined with advanced Castleloader malware, is installing Lumma "at scale."
